title: Travel cards in the UAE: 6 options compared
summary: In this guide, we’ll compare some popular travel cards in the UAE, break down their fees and features, and help you find the right option for you.
body_markdown:
If you’ve traveled outside of the UAE before, you’ve probably had this moment: you check your bank account after getting home and wonder why your trip cost more than you expected.


It often isn't the flights or hotels that catch you out. It's the small things. Paying for coffee, grabbing an Uber, shopping in a local market. Every time you swipe your everyday card, you might be adding more foreign transaction fees or currency conversion charges to your bill.


The good news is that there are plenty of travel cards designed to make spending overseas easier and more cost-effective nowadays. The challenge is knowing which one to choose.


That's where this guide comes in. We'll compare six of some popular travel cards available to UAE residents, break down their fees and features, and help you find the right option for the way you travel.

## How to choose the right card for spending abroad from the UAE


While there’s no ‘best’ card for spending abroad, finding the right one for you comes down to how you use it.


For example, before deciding on a card, ask:


- What do the conversion fees look like?


Using a regular UAE card abroad could sometimes cost you 2% – 3% per transaction in currency conversion fees. Travel cards, on the other hand, are designed to keep those costs lower – sometimes as low as 0%. It is also important to review subscription, ATM, card issuance and other applicable charges, as these may affect the overall cost.


- Are you a frequent flyer?


If you want to earn airline miles or get airport lounge access, look for a card that offers travel rewards and benefits that match the way you fly. Some providers partner with specific airlines, so it may be worth choosing a card linked to the airline you use most often.


- Do you often travel in the GCC area?


Depending on the provider, certain cards may offer more competitive fees when spending in neighboring GCC countries.


- Are you interested in brand discounts?


Some premium cards include perks like VPN access, free hotel stays, discounts for booking platforms, or complimentary travel insurance. These cards might also offer


[deals for UAE-based brands](https://ziina.com/personal/plans/violet) , which is great for when you aren’t traveling.


- What level of security is important to you?


Look for cards with easy app controls, instant freeze/unfreeze buttons, and fast customer support to protect against fraud. Virtual cards might also come with Face ID or virtual PIN numbers, which can add another layer of protection.


As a general rule, the right card is usually one that offers low currency conversion fees up to a limit that suits you, provides benefits that are important to you, and actually matches how often you travel.


Note: Make sure to check the minimum salary and eligibility requirements for each card, since that can quickly narrow down your options in the UAE.
